tasks.short: Prepare next week's lessons, write the week plan and materials, and show the plan when the school leader asks.

steps.what: Teacher reads the method's teacher guide for next week's lessons
Teacher checks last results and the group plan to decide changes
Teacher writes the week plan with goals, groups and activities to prepare classes
Teacher makes slides, worked examples and worksheets for the lessons

loop.input: Lesson goal, the teacher guide's key points and the class level from the week plan.
loop.output: Draft slide text, three worked examples and a short worksheet per lesson.
loop.check: Each item maps to the lesson's goal code; arithmetic answers are recomputed; a grade word list checks the language level; the teacher reads every item against the teacher guide for correctness and fit to the lesson and rewrites or drops items that do not fit.
loop.stop: One redraft per lesson; then the teacher writes it.
loop.why_not_simpler: Worked examples and explanations are new prose and numbers per lesson; a template cannot write them.

steps.what: Teacher saves the week plan in the shared folder for duo partner and substitutes
School leader asks for and reads the week plan during a class visit

tasks.design: A week-plan generator in {DOCS} pre-fills the school's template from the method's lesson sequence with goal codes, the timetable and the groups proposed from practice results in the {LMS}; the teacher edits it and it saves to the shared folder. A bounded model step drafts slides, worked examples and worksheets per lesson goal for the teacher to review.
tasks.previous_blocker: Week plans were typed from scratch because method data, timetable and results lived apart.
tasks.enabler_now: Methods publish lesson goals per lesson, templates can be filled from them, and trials show AI-assisted planning saves time without lower quality.
tasks.still_hard: Good preparation is thinking through the lesson; teachers in one trial used the AI tool for few lessons and less over time.
tasks.human_edge: Picturing how this class will react and choosing examples that fit these children.

ambition.what: Week plans that are current every Friday for duo partners and substitutes, not written after the fact for a visit.

tasks.altitude: The teacher edits a pre-filled plan and reviews drafted materials; preparation time shifts to thinking through the lesson.

reach.task: Teach from another teacher's week plan
reach.learn: Whether the pre-filled plan gives substitutes enough to teach from.

evidence.claim: A randomised trial with 259 secondary science teachers cut weekly planning from 81.5 to 56.2 minutes with a chatbot and a guide, with no quality difference.
A randomised trial with 464 primary teachers cut weekly preparation from 3.3 to 2.5 hours, but the assistant covered 7% of lessons and use declined.
An adaptive practice platform's assistant suggests arithmetic lessons that the teacher accepts or changes, piloted at a Dutch school board.
A school that adapts an AI tool can become its provider under the AI Act.

assumptions: Boundary: from reading the teacher guide to the week plan shared; teaching the lessons is outside.

Input contract: method lesson sequence with lesson goal and core-goal code per lesson, imported by the curriculum coordinator from the publisher's data; timetable from the school leader; groups from practice results in the {LMS}; fallback is the blank template.
No pupil data goes into the draft step; it works on lesson goals and teacher-guide text.
School leader time is outside the teacher's savings.
s3 keeps 60: the template is pre-filled with goals, timetable and proposed groups, but choosing activities and changes for the class stays with the teacher.
unknowns: Whether the method publisher's lesson data can be imported.
How much of the week plan the school requires.
research_questions: After ten weeks, for what share of lessons do teachers still use the drafted materials?

already_counted.description: Teacher checks and edits the pre-filled week plan.
Teacher reviews drafted slides, examples and worksheets before use.

incremental.description: Teacher reports wrong goal codes and poor drafts.
Curriculum coordinator imports method lesson data each year and keeps the template current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: as in the primary trial, teachers use the drafts for few lessons, so s4 keeps 90 and only the pre-filled week plan saving holds (24.6); high: drafts used for most lessons (32.9).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Show students how to use and care for scissors, tablets, kits and gym gear safely, and watch them use it.

steps.what: Teacher explains and demonstrates safe use and care of equipment
Teacher monitors students using equipment and corrects unsafe use
Teacher hands out and collects tablets and kits, checking for damage
Teacher reports damaged equipment: by e-mail today, in the damage form opened by the device's QR label with the device ID filled in after the change
Teacher checks the damage report before it goes: device, what is damaged and how it happened
Teacher submits the checked damage report to the ICT coordinator's queue
ICT coordinator logs the damage and arranges repair or replacement
Teacher records an injury: in the paper incident register today, in a form in the pupil records system after the change
Teacher writes the parent message about the injury: by phone or note today, by editing a message filled from the form after the change
Teacher checks the parent message before it goes: what happened, care given and the right parents
Teacher sends the checked message to the parents

tasks.design: A QR label on each tablet and kit opens a damage form with the device ID filled in; the teacher describes the damage, checks the report and submits it once as a ticket in the {HELPDESK} for the ICT coordinator. Injuries go into a form in the pupil records system ({OTHER}) that fills a parent message; the teacher edits and checks it and sends it once; teaching and supervision are unchanged.
tasks.previous_blocker: Damage and injuries were reported by e-mail and paper because the volumes are small.
tasks.enabler_now: QR labels and helpdesk forms take an afternoon to set up; records systems support custom forms and templates.
tasks.still_hard: Safety depends on the teacher's eyes in the room; no system watches thirty children with scissors.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing a risky moment before it happens and teaching care for shared things.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in decision rights; reporting takes less time.

reach.learn: Whether assistants use the QR damage form.

evidence.claim: A QR code on a device can open a pre-filled helpdesk form.
Injury records hold health data about pupils and follow the school's GDPR retention rules; reporting duties follow national rules.

assumptions: Boundary: from safety instruction to damage and injuries reported; repair and medical care are outside.
Input contract: device ID on a QR label, produced by the ICT coordinator when devices are registered; injury form fields set by the school leader; fallback is e-mail and paper.
No device tracking per pupil is added.
ICT coordinator time is outside the teacher's savings.

Recording an injury is a first record and keeps its full time; describing damage keeps 70 because only the device ID is filled in. The checks and sends of the damage report and the parent message keep their full time.
unknowns: How often equipment is damaged per term.
Whether the school already has a helpdesk for ICT.
research_questions: Does a damage form shorten the time a class is without a device?

already_counted.description: Teacher checks the filled parent message about an injury before sending.

incremental.description: ICT coordinator labels new devices and keeps the form current.

approvals.approved_version: The damage report with device ID, damage and cause exactly as checked by the teacher in s4b, submitted once as a ticket to the ICT coordinator's queue; any change needs a new check.
The parent message about this injury exactly as checked by the teacher in s6b, sent once to the pupil's parents through the pupil records system; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many labels are missing or damaged and parents are mostly phoned, so s4 keeps 90 and s6a keeps 100 (-0.2); high: labels and the message form used as designed (0.7).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Plan and schedule the period's lessons with the duo partner and parallel colleagues, following the curriculum.

steps.what: Teacher meets duo partner and parallel colleagues to divide and plan lessons
Teacher checks the method year plan for core-goal coverage
Teacher updates the shared planning spreadsheet: who teaches what, tests, trips
Teacher messages colleagues about swaps and schedule changes
School leader checks the period plans for curriculum coverage across groups

tasks.design: A shared period planner, a records app on the {PROJECT} or {DOCS} platform, starts from the method year plan with core-goal codes and the school calendar; teachers assign lessons, tests and trips, and the planner shows core-goal coverage and clashes per group. Changes notify the duo partner, and the school leader sees coverage across groups without collecting spreadsheets.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each team kept its own spreadsheet, and core-goal coverage was checked by reading method guides.
tasks.enabler_now: Methods publish year plans with goal codes, and a planner with a coverage view is a small records build.
tasks.still_hard: Dividing lessons is a negotiation between colleagues with different styles and part-time days.
tasks.human_edge: Agreeing with colleagues who does what, and adjusting the plan to what the children need.

ambition.what: Coverage gaps per group checked every period, not found at the end of the school year.

tasks.altitude: Teachers spend the meeting on choices, not on copying; the school leader sees coverage across groups.

reach.task: Check curriculum coverage across the school
reach.learn: Whether the planner's coverage view replaces their own checks.

evidence.claim: Core goals can be held as a fixed list and objectives mapped to a goal code.
Pupil records systems in Dutch primary schools track learning goals.

assumptions: Boundary: from the planning meeting to the period plan agreed; teaching is outside.

Input contract: method year plan with lesson, week and core-goal code, imported by the curriculum coordinator from publisher data; school calendar from the school leader; fallback is the spreadsheet; the previous period plan is the team's last shared planning.
No pupil data is involved.
School leader and colleagues' time is outside this teacher's savings.
The planning meeting keeps its full time; coverage and clash checks happen in the planner (s2, s3) and change messages shrink because changes show in the planner (s4).
unknowns: Whether method year plans are available with goal codes.
How many teachers share each group.
research_questions: How often are core goals missed in a year group today?

already_counted.description: Teacher reviews coverage gaps and clashes the planner flags.

incremental.description: Teacher keeps the planner current when plans change mid-period.
Curriculum coordinator imports year plans and keeps goal codes current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a teacher without a duo partner and one method per subject has little to share, so s3 keeps 80 and s4 keeps 90 (16.7); high: the planner used by the whole team (24.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Work with colleagues and school leaders to evaluate and revise school programmes, such as a reading method.

steps.what: Teacher joins working-group meetings on a school programme
Teacher exports test results per group and year into a spreadsheet
Teacher collects colleagues' experiences with the programme: by e-mail or talks today, by sending a short form with fixed questions after the change
Colleagues answer the short experience form
Teacher writes the programme evaluation and proposed revisions

loop.input: The results overview export, the survey summary and the working group's agreed points.
loop.output: A draft evaluation in the school's format: what was planned, results, colleague experience, proposed changes.
loop.check: Every number must match the results view; every claim cites a figure, a survey item or an agreed point, and the teacher checks that the claim follows from what it cites; proposals not in the agreed points are flagged for the teacher.
loop.stop: Two redrafts at most; then the teacher writes the evaluation.
loop.why_not_simpler: The evaluation is prose that weighs figures against colleagues' comments; a template only holds the headings.

steps.what: Teacher checks the final evaluation before it goes to the team: each figure and claim matches the results view and survey answers, and proposals are the agreed points
Teacher sends the checked evaluation to the school leader for the team meeting
School leader and team decide on revisions in the team meeting
Teacher updates the school's programme document after the decision
Teacher checks the revised programme document: it contains exactly the revisions decided in the team meeting
Teacher publishes the checked programme document to staff in the school's document space

tasks.design: A standard results view in {BI} on the school's pupil monitoring data shows results per subject, year and cohort, and a short {WORKFLOW} form collects colleagues' experience with fixed questions. A bounded model step drafts the evaluation from those two sources and the working group's points, checked against the figures, the teacher checks the evaluation and sends it to the school leader, and after the team's decision the teacher checks the revised programme and publishes it in {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each evaluation started with exporting results and chasing colleagues by e-mail, so evaluations were rare.
tasks.enabler_now: Pupil monitoring data can feed a standard dashboard, and language models draft prose from figures and notes with checks.
tasks.still_hard: Evaluating a programme is a team judgement; results per group can feel like judging teachers.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing what the figures mean in this school and bringing colleagues along to a change.

ambition.what: Each programme evaluated every year with the same view, instead of only when a method is replaced.

tasks.altitude: The teacher spends working-group time on interpretation and choices; the school leader decides from a consistent evaluation.

reach.learn: Whether one results view and form serve every programme evaluation.

evidence.claim: Dutch pupil records systems hold pupil results and learning-goal tracking.
Staff councils must consent to tools that can monitor staff, which can include results views per teacher's group.
AI that evaluates individual pupils' learning outcomes is high-risk; drafting a programme evaluation from group figures does not evaluate pupils.

assumptions: Boundary: from the working group's start to the revised programme published; implementing it in class is outside.

Input contract: test results per pupil and subject twice a year, produced by teachers entering or importing tests in the pupil records system; survey answers from colleagues; fallback is a manual export.
The results view shows groups and cohorts, not individual teachers, unless the staff council agrees.
School leader and colleagues' time is outside this teacher's savings.

s4 keeps 65 because the teacher reads and edits the drafted evaluation for meaning; colleagues' form answers are shown in s7 at share 1. Updating the programme document (s6) keeps its full time; the checks and sends keep theirs.
unknowns: Whether the school's test results can be exported to a dashboard.
How often programmes are evaluated now.
research_questions: Does a yearly evaluation lead to more or better-timed programme changes?

already_counted.description: Teacher checks the dashboard figures used for the evaluation.
Teacher checks and edits the drafted evaluation.

incremental.description: Teacher keeps survey questions current for each programme.
School board's data staff keep the results view and model service running.

approvals.approved_version: The programme evaluation with its figures, survey findings and proposals exactly as checked by the teacher in s4b, sent once to the school leader for the team meeting; any change needs a new check.

The programme document with exactly the revisions decided in s5, as checked by the teacher in s6b, published once to staff in the school's document space; any other change needs a new decision and check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a working group that meets mostly to discuss, few colleagues answer the form and the draft is barely used, so s3 and s4 keep 90 (11.6); high: results view, form and draft used as designed (19.9).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The teacher keeps teaching, supervising and the talks with colleagues; typing plans, copying results and writing evaluations from scratch shrink.
reach: Substitute teachers working from week plans
Instructional coordinators' coverage and quality checks
skills_to_grow: Reviewing drafted plans and materials quickly and critically
Reading results views for a group or programme
role.ambitious_version: A teacher whose week plans, period plans and evaluations are always current and shared, so colleagues and substitutes teach from the same picture.

job.title: Elementary School Teachers, Except Special Education
